title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
abstract: Opacity of mid- and high-$Z$ plasmas is dominated by thousands of overlapping spectral lines. Examples are laser-produced plasmas for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, inertial-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors. Radiation transport in such plasmas needs more than 1000 photon-energy groups in the EUV case, and this makes radiation-hydrodynamic simulations very expensive. We show that the accuracy of a small-group opacity model can be recovered by choosing properly \emph{which} fine bins are put into the same group. We present a data-driven method that assigns the fine bins of a detailed opacity and emissivity table to $K$ \emph{non-contiguous} groups. Each group has a fixed spectral shape inside it. The groups follow from one requirement: the reduced absorption operator must be diagonal for every plasma state. They are determined from a Gram matrix of spectra, taken from detailed-group solutions of a small part, for example 5\% in this work, of the parameter space. The reduced model is a set of $K$ uncoupled flux-limited diffusion equations. It can be used in an existing multigroup code by replacing the opacity table. For a Sn plasma with electron densities of $4\times10^{15}$--$1.1\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-3}$, electron temperatures of 5--250~eV, and scale lengths of 2.5--6900$\um$, the model with $K=100$ reproduces the total flux of the 1500-group reference with a median error of 2\% and a 90th-percentile error of 8\%. The 90th-percentile error is ten times smaller than that of a conventional 100-group model at the same cost.
